stories.headline: Naomi Osaka channels Allen Iverson in 2026 US Open debut
stories.summary: Naomi Osaka channeled Allen Iverson as part of her 2026 US Open debut Monday night as she beat Anastasia Zakharova 7-6 (6), 7-6 (3).
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Naomi Osaka channeled Allen Iverson as part of her 2026 US Open debut, and the former NBA superstar liked the look.

Osaka made her usual fashionable entrance for her match against Anastasia Zakharova on Monday night in the first round. The two-time US Open champion emerged from the tunnel onto the court in Arthur Ashe Stadium wearing a long white skirt and a gray, hooded robe featuring newspaper clippings about her.

She had the hood on when she entered. When she removed it to reveal her black outfit, Osaka had her hair done in cornrows under a headband, just as Iverson did when he was the NBA MVP while playing for the Philadelphia 76ers.

It fit with her apparel company's theme for the US Open after the New York Knicks won the NBA championship in June. Aryna Sabalenka is wearing an orange dress, one of the Knicks' colors.

"It's my, I guess, my tribute to Iverson. I really like him a lot," Osaka said following her 7-6 (6), 7-6 (3) victory. "I mean, Nike said basketball, so I said, 'OK, you want basketball, I'll give you basketball.'"

Osaka moved into the second round at Flushing Meadows with her 10th major match win this season, her most since 2019. It's the first time she has won a match at all four majors since 2018.

Osaka wore a shirt with Iverson's picture when she met with the media on the eve of the tournament and called him a trailblazer.

"I think he's also someone that I look up to a lot, because he's kind of like done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not, but he's shifted the way that NBA players dress," Osaka said Saturday. "I also think the whole conversation around clothes in sports and also just expressing yourself through style, I feel like he's someone that I look up to in that regard."

She added that they had never communicated, but Iverson posted a message to Osaka on his Instagram page Monday, writing: "Wow, what a honor!! BIG FAN can't wait to meet you."

ESPN Research and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Giants WR Nabers feeling 'good' but mum on playing Week 1
stories.summary: Malik Nabers is feeling "real good" ahead of the Giants' season opener against the Cowboys but remained noncommittal about playing Week 1.
stories.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Wide receiver Malik Nabers is feeling "real good" less than two weeks before the New York Giants' season opener against the Dallas Cowboys but remains noncommittal about playing Week 1.

Nabers is coming back from a torn ACL last year and has progressed to full practices throughout the summer. Everything seemingly has been trending in a positive direction.

"I feel pretty good. I feel real good to be honest," Nabers said. "Like I said, you're going to feel good but there's still some things that you're going to have to check off the box for you to participate. So I'm still going through that, still listening to the trainer, still listening to doctors and sharing everything with them."

Nabers said he was going to keep the final few checkpoints in-house. He added it wasn't anything too big.

But he did admit there was some uncertainty about whether he would be the pre-injury Nabers right away. Long term, however, that wasn't a concern.

"Will it take some time? Who knows?" he said. "But I know for sure if I'm out there, I'm going to run some routes."

The dynamic wide receiver has already been practicing in team drills this summer and recently shed the red no-contact jersey usually reserved for quarterbacks.

Still, he's not quite prepared to declare himself ready to play the Cowboys, even though the expectation is he will be playing barring some sort of setback. The Giants and Nabers have seemingly been gearing up for the Sunday night opener against Dallas on Sept. 13 since the first day of training camp.

"My mind is focused on playing the regular season. Playing whenever that is. Playing what[ever] team that is," Nabers said when asked if he was focusing on prepping for the Cowboys. "I'm going to be making sure that I'm ready to go out there and I'm healthy enough to play all four quarters and that nobody's got to make sure I'm not in on every play or they have to make sure I got enough snaps to play or my snaps are limited.

"So that's the main focus is just trying to be out there as much as I can."

Regardless of Nabers' role in Week 1, the Giants will have Odell Beckham Jr. back on the field at wide receiver for the first time in eight years. He made the 53-man roster on Sunday.

Coach John Harbaugh intends to use Beckham, whether it be as the fourth or fifth receiver.

"He'll be in that receiver group," Harbaugh said. "He'll be rotating in different personnel groups. He'll be playing."

Beckham had to earn that role with a strong summer, admitting there was unfamiliar pressure to win a job. It's something he has never experienced in his professional life.

After being out of the league for a year, making the Giants' roster was emotional, especially after having his family in town watching the final preseason game just days earlier.

"I had kind of those tears when I got back to the hotel after figuring out I'm going to be here," Beckham said. "It's an opportunity to rewrite some of the last bit of the chapters. Don't know [if this is the] last year [of my career] or whatever it is, I just know I'm going to give my all."

Beckham spent the first five seasons of his career with the Giants after being drafted with the 12th pick out of LSU. His career began with a bang, which included three straight seasons of at least 1,200 yards.

He did it all in the No. 13 jersey he made famous. But Beckham has worn No. 3 this summer while Jalin Hyatt has 13.

Beckham said there will be a "conversation" about that now that he has made the team and Hyatt sits on the practice squad.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton takes ownership of iconic Ferrari F40 road car
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has taken ownership of a Ferrari F40 road car after it sat dormant in a garage for over 30 years.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has taken ownership of a Ferrari F40 road car after it sat dormant in a garage for over 30 years.

The iconic supercar was in production from 1987 to 1992, with roughly 1,315 examples rolling out of Maranello's factory gates in that period.

Although Hamilton has been a Ferrari Formula 1 driver for over 18 months, he has been waiting for the perfect F40 to invest in and appears to have found a rare low-mileage example.

The seven-time champion's time at Maranello is already synonymous with the car after he posed for a photo with one on his arrival at Ferrari at the start of 2025.

He also posted a video of himself driving a Japanese-based F40 at a Tokyo car meet earlier this year.

Posting on Instagram on Monday, Hamilton introduced the car as his "very own F40," adding "this is the car of my dreams."

The post included a series of images of the dust-covered car at Ferrari's "classiche" department, which restores and certifies Ferraris that are over 20 years old.

- Lando Norris signs new contract to stay at McLaren until at least 2030

- Lewis Hamilton: Sarcastic Ferrari radio messages not 'best version of me'

"These cars are works of art and incredibly rare, so when I found this one, covered in dust after being sat in a garage for over thirty years, I knew I had to bring her home," Hamilton wrote.

"First to Maranello, where the master engineers and mechanics at the factory worked for weeks to bring her back to life. Massive thank you to everyone who had a hand in this project. This has truly been a dream come true."

Hamilton has owned numerous expensive cars over the years, but in 2025 revealed he had sold his collection which, at various times, included a one-off Pagani Zonda 760 LH, a Ferrari LaFerrari and a 1966 Shelby Cobra.

Speaking at last year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, he said he was "more into art" than cars but would still consider an F40, which Hamilton described as "a piece of art."

Ferrari F40s have been known to gather prices in excess of $8 million at auction, but values vary based on condition, mileage and specification.

The V8-turbo supercar is significant in the brand's history as it was the last of its road cars to be commissioned and approved by founder Enzo Ferrari before his death in 1988.

Original owners include F1 legends Niki Lauda, Jacky Ickx, Gerhard Burger, John Surtees and Striling Moss.

Hamilton's former on track rival, Sebastian Vettel, owned an F40 that previously belonged to Luciano Paravrotti, although he reportedly sold it after he left the Italian team in 2020, saying he wanted more "space."

It remains to be seen whether Hamilton will arrive at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix in his freshly restored F40.

stories.headline: Sources: Southampton loans USMNT's Downs to St. Louis
stories.summary: St. Louis City SC is set to acquire United States forward Damion Downs on loan from English Championship side Southampton, a source with direct knowledge of the deal confirmed to ESPN.
stories.body:
St. Louis City SC is set to acquire United States forward Damion Downs on loan from English Championship side Southampton, a source with direct knowledge of the deal confirmed to ESPN.

Downs, 22, is looking for a fresh start after failing to find the net for the Saints since the club acquired him in July of 2025. He has yet to appear for the club in the Championship so far this season.

The U.S. international appeared to be on the rise after scoring 11 goals in all competitions for FC Cologne during the 2024-25 season. A spot with the USMNT for the 2025 Gold Cup followed, and he scored the winning penalty in the shootout victory over Costa Rica in the quarterfinals.

But Downs' last goal at club level came during the aforementioned campaign with Cologne. Not even a return to the Bundesliga last season on loan with Hamburg SV, which saw him make 12 appearances, was enough to revive his fortunes.

Downs will find the competition for places intense given the team's likely capture of Colorado Rapids forward Rafael Navarro. St. Louis has also been among the hotter teams in MLS, having gone unbeaten in its last 12 league matches, and moving up to sixth place in the Western Conference.

Downs has made a total of six appearances for the USMNT. He was born in Germany to an American father and German mother and spent some of his childhood in the United States.

The Athletic was the first to report the news of Downs' loan to St. Louis.

stories.headline: EFL criticises UEFA after rescheduling three domestic fixtures
stories.summary: The English Football League has accused UEFA of an "unwillingness to cooperate" after it says the European governing body's stance forced them to rearrange three domestic fixtures.
stories.body:
The English Football League has accused UEFA of an "unwillingness to cooperate" after it says the European governing body's stance forced them to rearrange three domestic fixtures.

Everton and Wolves were scheduled to play their Carabao Cup third-round tie on Sept. 9 before Liverpool and Atlético Madrid's Champions League clash was, on Saturday, announced for the same day.

As a result, that contest and two others -- Liverpool and Tottenham in the League Cup and Wolves vs. Portsmouth in the Championship -- have been rescheduled.

An EFL statement read: "On Saturday, UEFA announced that it had scheduled Liverpool v Atlético Madrid for the same date, despite it being clear that Everton and Liverpool cannot play home fixtures on the same evening.

"The EFL met with UEFA officials on Monday morning to explore available options, however in those discussions it was made clear that they were unwilling to consider rescheduling the Liverpool v Atlético Madrid fixture due to the impact on supporters travelling from overseas.

"Disappointingly, the League has therefore been forced to make changes.

"Over recent seasons the League has made a number of changes to accommodate the expansion of UEFA Club competitions -- a decision which was made without adequate consultation with domestic leagues.

"These changes have included splitting Carabao Cup round three ties across two weeks, and implementing draw conditions for round three which prevent scheduling conflicts for clubs playing in the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League.

- Champions League draw becomes UEFA's latest stand against FIFA president Infantino

- Champions League draw: Good games for Liverpool, bad for Barcelona

"This makes UEFA's unwillingness to cooperate all the more frustrating, not least for the supporters of the five impacted clubs, and we sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused."

UEFA, in response, insisted it "always does its best to accommodate reasonable requests", but said the "potential conflict" only emerged after fixtures were published, when changes were no longer possible.

The European governing body said in a statement: "UEFA regularly receives scheduling requests from associations, leagues and clubs and always does its best to accommodate reasonable requests wherever possible.

"In this case, no issue had been raised with UEFA during the scheduling process, and the potential conflict only became apparent after the publication of the fixture lists.

"At that stage, it was not possible to make changes, particularly given the significant number of supporters who may already have arranged international travel and accommodation. We believe that these commitments deserve to be respected.

"UEFA remains in contact with the relevant stakeholders, and we appreciate all efforts to minimise any local operational challenges."

Everton vs. Wolves is now set for Wednesday, Sept. 16; Liverpool vs. Tottenham, originally slated for Sept. 16, is now a day earlier and Wolves vs. Portsmouth, also initially due to be played on Sept. 16, will take place on Oct. 20.

stories.headline: Song Yadong KO's Umar Nurmagomedov in massive UFC upset
stories.summary: Song Yadong pulled off a massive upset by knocking out heavily favored Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night in Shanghai.
stories.body:
Song Yadong saved the greatest performance of his career for his home country, knocking out former title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Shanghai.

Song (24-9-1, 1 NC), a nearly 5-1 underdog at DraftKings Sportsbook, dropped Nurmagomedov with a short right hand, drawing a roar from the crowd when the fight was waved off at 1 minute, 48 seconds of Round 2.

"I believe in myself, and my team believed that I would win this fight," Song said through an interpreter. "They told me I would knock this guy out, and I did it."

It was the second straight fight in China for Song and his second straight win by finish. His most recent knockout win had been in 2023.

Song, making his first appearance in Shanghai since his UFC debut at age 19 in 2017, walked out to a hero's welcome.

"Nine years ago, I wanted to show I could walk in this Octagon," he said. "Nine years later, I want to prove I am the best in the world. I am the best Chinese fighter in the world."

The knockout came after Nurmagomedov (20-2) ducked out of the way of a left hand and right into the path of a short right hand, which connected near his right ear and sent him limply to the canvas. Song delivered three finishing shots on the mat before the referee jumped in.

That sent Song running around inside the cage in celebration, where he nearly ran into Nurmagomedov's younger brother and cornerman, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, who had rushed in to check on his fallen brother. Usman Nurmagomedov appeared to throw an elbow in Song's direction as the elated winner was running past.

Song climbed atop the cage to soak in the fans' cheers before jumping down outside the cage and running into the crowd to get hugs and high-fives from fans.

"Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not next month, but I will be the first male Chinese UFC champion," Song said through the interpreter, with the "male" designation a nod to countrywoman Zhang Weili, a two-time women's champion at strawweight.

Song, who trains in Sacramento, California, switched to English and yelled, "Give me the title shot!"

stories.headline: Jets star goalie Connor Hellebuyck confirms trade request
stories.summary: Three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly confirmed Thursday that he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him.
stories.body:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba -- Three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly confirmed Thursday that he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him.

In a statement released by his agent, Ray Petkau, Hellebuyck said he made the request several months ago and "tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options."

Hellebuyck said he felt it was important to go public because training camp is fast approaching. Camps are set to open in roughly three weeks.

"My position has not changed, and I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family," Hellebuyck said. "(I) hope a resolution can be reached soon."

Hellebuyck, 33, has played his entire NHL career with the Jets and was voted MVP in the 2024-25 season. He backstopped the U.S. to the gold medal at the Olympics in February.

A team spokesperson did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.

Trade rumors swirled about Hellebuyck in late June around the draft, but nothing came to fruition. The Michigan native missed time because of injury and had a career-worst .895 save percentage last season as Winnipeg underachieved expectations and missed the playoffs.

But his track record and body of work are among the best at the position over the past decade. His 345 wins, 2.58 goals-against average and .916 save percentage since entering the league in 2015 are second only to Tampa Bay two-time Stanley Cup champion Andrei Vasilevskiy.

Hellebuyck has not enjoyed the same postseason success as Vasilevskiy and the Lightning. He's 24-34, with the Jets only making it past the second round and into the Western Conference final once, back in 2018.

He signed an eight-year, $59.5 million extension with Winnipeg in October 2023. He's under contract through 2031 at a salary cap hit of $8.5 million.

"Winnipeg has been my home for my entire NHL career, and I will always be grateful for my time there," Hellebuyck said. "I appreciate everything Winnipeg Jets fans have meant to me throughout my career."

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail R27: Dragons prop Blake Lawrie in Super League switch
stories.summary: Blake Lawrie will earn a rare start this weekend before he heads off to join the Super League, while the future of his Dragons teammate Tyrell Sloan is still a little uncertain.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into Round 27 of the NRL.

Lawrie lands new club

170-game Dragons veteran Blake Lawrie has landed his next destination, with sources informing ESPN that he's agreed to a three-year deal with the York Knights in the Super League.

After it was announced by St George Illawarra that he'd be departing the club at the end of the 2026 season, ESPN can reveal he is bound for England.

He had garnered interest from the Catalans Dragons, before opting to sign with the Knights.

Lawrie will be named in the No. 10 jumper for the Red V in his final game as a Dragon this weekend.

Sloan's future may yet be in red and white

Doubt has clouded Tyrell Sloan's move to the Castleford Tigers in 2027, and while he says he "still signed a contract" and intends to honour it at his next club, the prospect of returning to the Dragons remains a possibility to him.

"Honestly, my manager works hard, and he's really good at his job," he said when asked if there's any conversations around a potential backflip to remain at the Red V.

"Whatever happens, it's going to be for the best reason and again, I've signed a contract, so I do want to make that clear."

He went on to say he hopes that this weekend won't be his last as a Dragon.

stories.headline: From Knicks to Yankees, Nick Jonas finds the perfect song
stories.summary: The Jonas Brothers are longtime New York sports fans and have a song that can speak to their favorite teams.
stories.body:
First, it was the New York Knicks' first NBA title in 53 years. Then it was the "American royal wedding" between pop star Taylor Swift and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce keeping the historic Madison Square Garden busy this summer. However, summer at the world's most famous arena isn't over yet.

The Jonas Brothers' three-night stint at MSG for the "Burnin' Up Tour All Over Again" kicks off Aug. 20. Raised in New Jersey, the three brothers, who are featured in the new Disney film "Camp Rock 3," are New York sports fans and have been unwavering supporters of the Knicks, so the venue just seems fitting, especially during a summer like this.

"Going back to last year, the run [the Knicks] made in the playoffs, I was in New York at the time doing a show on Broadway and was around it every day, feeling the energy in the city. It was electric," Jonas told ESPN. "Cut to this year, and just to see them complete the journey during the finals and what that meant to the city as a whole ... it was pretty incredible to see."

On the crest of a historic New York summer and ahead of performing at halftime of the NFL Week 1 game between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, ESPN spoke with Nick Jonas and he assigned songs to his favorite teams. Jonas and comedian Kevin Hart headline DraftKings' "Take Your Game Anywhere" campaign that launches on Sept. 2.

New York Knicks: 'Love Bug'

Again, the Knicks are still the moment after winning their first NBA championship in more than 50 years. This sweet ballad from the Jonas Brothers, released in 2008, perfectly sums up how Nick Jonas feels about his team.

"It just feels right for them," he said.

New York Giants: 'Sucker'

The NFL regular season is right around the corner, and many New York sports fans are loyal to "Big Blue." The Giants also have a humongous fanbase, just like "Sucker." In 2019, the group's comeback single struck the top of the Billboard charts -- the Jonas Brothers' first-ever No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

"I'm probably going to go with 'Sucker' because it's the biggest one, the most important [song], to some," Jonas told ESPN.

New York Yankees: 'Burnin' Up'

Just like the Yankees, there's so much nostalgia that comes with "Burnin' Up." The song, released in 2008, was one of the first smash hits for the Jonas Brothers. As for the Yankees, they are one of the most revered franchises in sports.

"[The Yankees are] more like legacy," Jonas said.

stories.headline: Colton Cowser saves Orioles with incredible catch to preserve 2-1 victory over Rockies
stories.summary: — Colton Cowser made a spectacular leaping catch above the center-field fence for the final out, robbing Jake McCarthy of a game-winning homer and preserving the Baltimore Orioles' 2-1 victory over the Colorado Rockies on Monday night.
stories.body:
DENVER -- — Colton Cowser made a spectacular leaping catch above the center-field fence for the final out, robbing Jake McCarthy of a game-winning homer and preserving the Baltimore Orioles' 2-1 victory over the Colorado Rockies on Monday night.


Cade Povich pitched five solid innings and Cowser drove in the go-ahead run in the seventh following a 98-minute rain delay at Coors Field.


Baltimore (69-69) has won four straight and six of seven to reach .500 for the first time since taking the first game of a doubleheader against Houston 10-3 on April 30. The surging Orioles moved within a half-game of idle Cleveland in the crowded chase for the last American League wild card.


The Rockies have lost five in a row overall and a franchise-record 10 straight at home, the longest home losing streak in the majors this season.


The game was paused between the fifth and sixth due to heavy rain and lightning in the area.


Blaze Alexander walked to load the bases with one out in the seventh before Cowser grounded into a fielder’s choice that gave the Orioles a 2-1 lead. Cowser was initially ruled out at first base for what would have been an inning-ending double play, but the call was challenged by the Orioles and overturned.


Grant Wolfram (6-2) pitched two scoreless innings in relief for the win. Andrew Kittredge earned his ninth save this season.


Povich allowed five hits and one run.


Following the rain delay, Mark Manfredi (1-1) replaced Rockies starter Tanner Gordon, who allowed one run in five innings. Manfredi walked three and gave up one run in 1 1/3 innings.


Dylan Beavers hit a leadoff double in the Baltimore fifth and scored two pitches later when Samuel Basallo hit a towering double off the wall in right-center.


Hunter Goodman doubled leading off the fourth for Colorado and scored on a two-out single by Jordan Beck to make it 1-0.


Up next
Orioles RHP Kyle Bradish (7-12, 4.03 ERA) starts Tuesday opposite Rockies RHP Gabriel Hughes (0-6, 6.61).

stories.headline: Minter backs Loop as Ravens add kicker competition in Moody
stories.summary: Baltimore signed Jake Moody to the practice squad three days after Tyler Loop missed two kicks in the preseason finale.
stories.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens coach Jesse Minter backed Tyler Loop as his kicker Monday even after adding competition for his job.

Baltimore signed Jake Moody to the practice squad three days after Loop missed two kicks in the preseason finale and heard boos from the M&T Bank Stadium crowd. Loop, who finished 5-of-8 (62.5%) in the preseason, is looking to rebound from missing a 44-yard, last-second attempt that abruptly ended Baltimore's season eight months ago.

"I have a lot of confidence in Tyler still," Minter said after Monday's practice. "He's had a great training camp. I expect him to be our kicker going into [the Sept. 13 season opener in] Indianapolis."

Minter added, "But you're always trying to just have every scenario covered. And so that's what we're trying to do as a team."

The Ravens showed their confidence in Loop this offseason by not bringing in another kicker throughout spring workouts and training camp. Loop missed only a handful of kicks over 20 practices this summer.

But Loop had an uneven preseason, missing kicks from 49, 51 and 58 yards and leading to speculation about his job security.

Moody, 26, joins the Ravens' practice squad about two weeks after being released by the Washington Commanders. He lost the kicking battle with undrafted rookie Drew Stevens after struggling in training camp, where he missed 4 of 6 kicks during one practice.

A third-round pick by the San Francisco 49ers in 2023 -- the highest drafted kicker over the past decade -- Moody has converted 64 of 82 career field goals for the 49ers, Chicago Bears and Commanders. His success rate of 78% ranks 31st among kickers with at least 50 field goal attempts since 2023.

Last season, Moody was cut by San Francisco after he missed two of three field goal tries in the opener. He then made 18 of 20 field goal attempts (90%) for the Bears and Commanders.

There is a connection between Moody and Minter. Moody's final season at the University of Michigan was 2022, when Minter was the defensive coordinator there.

"Jake's just kind of been on the radar," Minter said. "He's a guy that's had success in this league and really just felt like adding a guy. It's whatever's best for the team at that particular moment. So we added a guy to compete on the practice squad and see how it shakes out from there."

In other news, Minter said he expects Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike to play early this season. Madubuike missed the final 15 weeks of last season because of a neck injury, which required surgery in April.

The Ravens decided not to place Madubuike on injured reserve Saturday because that would have forced him to miss the first four games of the regular season.

"I don't see him, obviously, missing that many games," Minter said.

stories.headline: AFL overreactions: Will Pendlebury's legacy be tarnished with a move to the Suns?
stories.summary: The big news this week was that Scott Pendlebury would depart Collingwood and join Gold Coast on a playing-then-coaching deal. But will this move tarnish his legacy as a Collingwood and AFL legend? Let's get to this week's big talking point.
stories.body:
There are plenty of talking points after the AFL's wildcard weekend, with one of the biggest being the announcement Scott Pendlebury would depart Collingwood and join Gold Coast likely on a playing-then-coaching deal.

Let's get to this week's overreactions column, where we judge the biggest takeaways as legitimate or irrational.

Scott Pendlebury's legacy will be tarnished by not being a one-club player
The football world was left stunned on Sunday morning when news broke that Collingwood champion Scott Pendlebury would be departing the club and continuing his playing career at Gold Coast.

It's understood the 442-game veteran was eager to remain at the Magpies but a contract extension reportedly never arrived, leading Pendlebury to explore other playing opportunities for 2027. With his move to the Suns now all but confirmed, he is no longer set to be the one-club player many believed he would retire as, and that's led to questions and concerns about his legacy.

Verdict: Overreaction

So what if Pendlebury isn't a one-club player. Sam Mitchell isn't a one-club player and nobody would associate him with any club other than Hawthorn. Luke Hodge's name carries the same weight around Hawthron even though he finished his career at the Lioins. It's also easy to forget that Nathan Buckley once upon a time played for Brisbane.

Pendlebury has built up enough credits over his 20-year career where his legendary footballing legacy is secure. There's pretty much nothing he can do that would taint his image as one of the most revered and respected players in league history.

It's 2026, and the long-held concept of player loyalty isn't the same as it once was. With football being the business it is, loyalty can often be a one-way street. It's always a savvy and responsible move for players to look after their futures.

Extending his career at another club certainly shouldn't be viewed as a negative. In fact, who's to say taking this path won't ultimately enhance his legacy?

What would a premiership at the Suns mean for Pendlebury? It has to add to his story in a positive way. I'm not saying that's happening next season but it proves his legacy is still being written.

-- Jake Michaels

stories.headline: How A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum injuries impact USA at World Cup
stories.summary: How will the deepest roster in the world make up for A'ja Wilson's absence? And what might be next for Kelsey Plum?
stories.byline: Alexa Philippou and Michael Voepel and Kareem Copeland
stories.body:
Basketball fans woke to stunning news Monday with the announcement that A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum will not participate in the upcoming FIBA Women's World Cup due to health issues.

Plum's absence isn't entirely surprising; she has been limited to 17 games this summer while dealing with a lower leg injury and appeared in just five contests since being traded to the Phoenix Mercury, who on Monday also ruled her out for the remainder of the WNBA season.

Wilson is a different story. She had been listed as dealing with a back issue going into the Las Vegas Aces' most recent two games but didn't miss either contest.

Largely regarded as the best player in the world, Wilson has been a stalwart of USA Basketball, making her debut for the senior national team in a major international competition at the 2018 World Cup. She is the reigning MVP of the 2022 World Cup and the 2024 Olympics, leading the U.S. women in scoring at both events.

Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron, announced Monday as replacement players for Wilson and Plum, are already in Berlin with Team USA as it prepares for Friday's opening group-phase game against China.

ESPN analyzes what the news means for the U.S. women as they go for their fifth consecutive World Cup gold medal.

What do we know about Wilson's health status?

Alexa Philippou: Wilson has been largely dominant this WNBA season, well within reach of a potential fifth WNBA MVP award, even as she hasn't had a fully clean bill of health. In late June/early July, Wilson missed three games (including the Commissioner's Cup final) with an ankle injury. Then the back issue popped up on the injury report twice in the past week, though Wilson appeared in both games, including playing 30 minutes Friday in the Aces' final contest before the FIBA break. Along with USA teammates Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young, she also sat out Las Vegas' Aug. 9 matchup against the New York Liberty (the second game of a back-to-back) to rest.

Durability has been a hallmark of Wilson's historic WNBA career; prior to this season, she had missed just six regular-season games over the past seven seasons. She has also prioritized not playing overseas during WNBA offseasons, which has helped her avoid additional wear and tear.

But a source close to the situation told ESPN on Monday that Wilson hasn't been 100% for some time now with those back issues, and that there was a concern the FIBA schedule could exacerbate her situation.

Interestingly, Wilson indicated as early as late July that she'd been weighing what was best for her and her body when it came to balancing USA Basketball commitments with the Aces' grueling August schedule (and ultimate playoff push).

"I have given it some thought, not going to lie," Wilson told "The Dunker Spot." "It has been a thought of mine, just to see how to navigate it all and just the prioritization that would need to go into that. I'm going to see when it gets to that moment and how I feel. My body will tell it all."

What does Wilson's absence mean for USA Basketball?

Philippou: Losing two important veterans and key contributors to Team USA's recent success is far from ideal. The World Cup is notoriously difficult due to its grueling schedule -- Team USA plays three games in four days to start the event and -- assuming it advances to the final day of competition -- six in 10. This is all with very little prep time as Kara Lawson embarks on her first major international competition as head coach of the senior national team.

No matter how deep the USA talent pool is, losing the best player in the world is a major blow. Wilson averaged a double-double (18.7 PPG, 10.2 RPG, 2.7 BPG) in just over 27 minutes per game at the 2024 Paris Olympics, which included a 21-point, 13-rebound, four-block effort versus France in the gold medal game. Plum also is experienced at both the World Cup and Olympic levels and was a key player off the bench who helped stymie France's upset bid.

Though there was no U.S. training camp stateside heading into the World Cup, Lawson led the team in the World Cup qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico in March. Eight of the 12 members of that roster are now on the Berlin squad: Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark, Kahleah Copper, Gray, Rhyne Howard, Iriafen, Angel Reese and Young. That should provide a level of familiarity to players, the coaching staff and Lawson's system amid so much newness.

One thing to note is that Aliyah Boston has been playing through a right leg injury that has kept her out of some Fever games this year; it's worth monitoring how USA Basketball manages her minutes in light of Wilson's absence and a strenuous schedule.

Is there a precedent for Team USA losing such a key player so close to a major event?

Michael Voepel: Yes. In the 2006 World Cup (then called the world championship), Los Angeles Sparks center Lisa Leslie was a late scratch because her uncle had been seriously injured in a car accident. Leslie was the WNBA MVP that year and had been Team USA's star post player for a decade. The Americans missed having her in that World Cup, losing in the semifinals to Russia and then taking the bronze medal by beating host Brazil.

That is the U.S. women's only loss in the two major international competitions -- the Olympics and World Cup -- since 1994.

While Leslie's absence was due to a family emergency, Wilson's is due to health issues and the decision to avoid the extra physical demands of an in-season tournament. That won't be the case after this World Cup, though. The WNBA season and international events have long caused scheduling conflicts, resulting in either a compacted WNBA season (which allowed players less rest), a midseason break like this year or holding the World Cup shortly after the conclusion of the WNBA season. In 2022, for example, the World Cup started Sept. 22, four days after the Finals concluded.

But starting in 2030, the World Cup is changing its calendar footprint. That year in Japan, it will be held from Nov. 26 to Dec. 8, after the WNBA season is over.

The World Cup's move to late November-early December in 2030 should be the best compromise. However, the WNBA regular season expands to 50 games next year, so the Finals might not be over until November in 2030.

Without Wilson and Plum, who will have to step for Team USA?

Kareem Copeland: As much as we'll look to the established veterans to pick up the slack for the loss of four combined Olympic gold medals, all of a sudden there's an opportunity for the Young and Turnt Corps. Outside of Breanna Stewart, the only true bigs on the roster are Boston, Reese and Iriafen. The perimeter is deeper with established veterans, but one fewer guard opens up minutes that could be capitalized on by Bueckers or Clark. Even the addition of Citron gives the Americans an uberefficient, defensive-minded perimeter talent to play matchup games with. Team USA has the deepest roster in the world and has begun to work in the young future of the roster. Plum's absence opens some opportunities that could be grabbed by the youngsters.

Philippou: Even more will be on the veterans' shoulders, particularly Stewart's. Not only is she the most experienced big on the roster, but Stewart is also the most experienced player with USA Basketball, period, boasting three Olympic and three World Cup gold medals in her career. The leadership transition might have begun in 2022 and 2024, with Sue Bird and Diana Taurasi either limited or not participating in that World Cup and Olympics, but now Stewart clearly takes the mantle as the experienced vet tasked with carrying on USA Basketball's tradition of excellence. Fortunately, she won't be entirely alone, as Young, Gray, Copper and Napheesa Collier have all won at least one gold medal with USA Basketball at a major international competition.

What's next for Kelsey Plum?

Copeland: Health and free agency. The start to 2026 was fantastic for Plum as she averaged 26.6 points through her first 10 games of the season, including a 43-point masterpiece on June 13, which had her on pace to earn the first scoring title of her career. Little did we know that she'd be traded and play a total of seven more games after that opening 10. Plum said it herself on social media Monday: The decision was made to "focus on getting my body back to 100%." Stepping out of the World Cup firmly puts the focus on the future.

That future, however, is unknown beyond the calf injury that has been an issue all summer. The Mercury traded a 2027 first-round draft pick, 2028 second-round draft pick and a young, talented guard in Monique Akoa Makani still on a rookie contract for five games of Plum, who is on a one-year deal. The question is, will that and an upcoming offseason in Phoenix be enough to convince the 32-year-old to stay? The facilities are some of the best in the WNBA, and Alyssa Thomas, Copper and Sami Whitcomb are all signed through the 2027 season. Is that enough to convince Plum to stay when other teams will tempt her with plenty of cash and a chance to win a ring?

stories.headline: Premier League VAR review: Arsenal should've been awarded a penalty, so why did VAR let it go?
stories.summary: VAR often causes Premier League controversy, but how are decisions made and are they correct? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
stories.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a World Cup matchday.

Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal (Aug. 31)
Referee: Jarred Gillett

VAR: James Bell

Time: 90 + 9 mins

Incident: Possible penalty to Arsenal

What happened: Arsenal's Bruno Guimarães was screaming for a penalty after he was challenged from behind by Villa's Ian Maatsen inside the box. Referee Jarred Gillett waved away the appeals.

VAR decision: VAR checked and cleared the on-field decision of no penalty.

VAR review: VAR James Bell clearly applied the new "high bar" for intervention when he cleared this decision, taking the view that the referee's on-field decision not to award a penalty to Arsenal was not a clear and obvious error. After reviewing the replays, VAR quickly checked and cleared the decision as correct.

Verdict and insight: For me, this was a clear penalty kick that should've been awarded to Arsenal. I was surprised it was not given on-field by match referee Gillett, and equally surprised the VAR did not recommend a pitch-side review.

The decision by Villa's Maatsen to challenge in the nature he did, from behind with a scissor action and no opportunity to play the ball was a poor one. By making contact only with Guimarães and none on the ball, there can be little doubt that it met the threshold for a foul -- and it took place inside the penalty box.

The surprising non-intervention by VAR is a result of the Premier League's desire this season to have less involvement and only very clear errors to be corrected, with a new "higher bar" for interventions to be applied.

It's a positive principle that should result in less time spent re-litigating decisions, yes. However, this was clearly a mistake from the on-field referee not to award a penalty and, in my opinion, this was an intervention that has been missed by the VAR team.

Arsenal winning the game will cover the narrative to some degree, however, if this was a deciding moment that cost Arsenal all three points, the profile of the incident would've been significant.

The high bar will absolutely improve the game and lower the expectations from football that VAR should get involved in everything, however it is so important that clear fouls in the penalty area, like this situation, do not get overlooked when the referee has mis-read a key moment.

Manchester United 5-2 Ipswich Town (Aug. 30)
Referee: Craig Pawson

VAR: Jarred Gillett

Time: 56th minute

Incident: Possible handball in lead-up to Man United's second goal by Harry Maguire

What happened: The ball was cleared out of Ipswich's box toward Maguire, and the ball appeared to strike the arm of Maguire. He brought the ball to his feet and struck the ball toward goal, where it then took a grave deflection from Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves before going into the goal. Following a VAR review, the goal was allowed to stand.

VAR decision and communications: The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR, who deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.

VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal."

VAR review: With the knowledge that the ball had clearly struck the arm of Maguire, the VAR had two key elements to consider:

(1) Was Maguire's shot on target before it struck Greaves and entered the goal? In other words: was Maguire the goalscorer?

(2) Was the handball by Maguire accidental or a punishable as an intentional handball offence?

The answers to both questions could have resulted in a different outcome, but the VAR determined that it was clearly an own goal by Greaves, meaning Maguire was not the scorer, and that the handball incident was accidental. Both details meant the ball striking the arm of Maguire was negated in law, and the VAR recommended to the referee that the goal should be awarded.

Verdict and insight: It's understandable that Ipswich Town will feel hard-done by the decision.

If Maguire had scored the goal, then his handling of the ball in the lead-up would've canceled out the goal. It's only because it took the massive deflection that changed the trajectory of the ball that Maguire's incidental handball did not result in the goal being overturned.

In truth, it was a 50/50 decision that could have fallen the other way if the judgement of VAR was a different one. But the law doesn't allow a goal to be disallowed in this situation if the handball by Maguire was judged as accidental.

The subjective nature of handball in general is a confusing element of the game, and if VAR had judged this as a punishable handball and disallowed the goal, it would certainly have been a credible outcome given the context of the situation in my opinion -- and a more comfortable outcome for football.

However, the judgement by VAR Jared Gillett was not an incorrect one, with Maguire challenging for a bouncing ball and his arms in front of his body, the ball striking his left arm can certainly be deemed as accidental. It was on this occasion, with Man United the benefactor of it in this situation, and Ipswich rightfully feeling hard done by.

Newcastle United 2-2 Liverpool (Aug. 23)
Referee: Stuart Attwell

VAR: James Bell

Time: 90 + 6 mins

Incident: Penalty awarded to Liverpool for a challenge by Lewis Hall on Victor Muñoz

What happened: Liverpool's Muñoz charged into the Newcastle penalty area late into the game, and Hall made a clumsy challenge bringing the Liverpool player to the ground. Referee Stuart Attwell pointed to the spot for a late penalty for the Reds.

VAR decision and communications: The referee's call of penalty for the challenge by Hall on Muñoz was checked and confirmed by VAR.

The referee: "He doesn't play the ball. He makes clear contact."

VAR: "It's knee into thigh contact. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty."

Verdict: This was a correct decision made by referee Atwell and his assistant, and a decision I felt was clear in real-time.

In this type of situation, with an attacker moving into the penalty area at speed with the ball under control, any challenge by a defender must successfully play the ball or they run a very high risk of committing a foul.

Hall was naïve to make his clumsy challenge in the manner he did, and Muñoz was too clever for the Newcastle defender. This was a clear foul by Hall, and a penalty kick a correct outcome.

While it may feel to Newcastle fans that Liverpool were bailed out and gifted a draw after middling performance, Hall's foul was needless and to blame for Liverpool equalizing.

stories.headline: What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is facing 100 drivers in a unique event called Max vs. 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 challengers, starting from the back of the grid.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is taking part in a unique event called Max vs 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 drivers, starting from the back of the grid.

The 28-year-old currently races in F1, the highest tier in motorsport. He is one of the fiercest competitors out there and is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking.

But if you have never heard of him, or want to learn more, here is everything you need to know.

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

Who is Max Verstappen?
Verstappen was born in Belgium to his Dutch father Jos and his Belgian mother Sophie. His father raced in F1 between 1994-2003 and had two podium finishes, while his mother competed in karts. He currently resides in Monaco.

Who does he race for?
Verstappen started racing go-karts when he was just four years old and started to compete in championships at seven.

He then made his way through the ranks winning several world and European titles in 2013. He raced just one season in Formula 3 before skipping Formula 2 and heading straight to Formula 1.

In 2015, he signed for Red Bull junior team Toro Rosso at the age of 17 before he was promoted to Red Bull a year later.

He then went on to become the youngest ever grand prix winner after taking victory at the Spanish Grand Prix and has been at Red Bull ever since, becoming the most successful driver at the team.

He signed a long-term contract back in March 2022 to stay at the Milton Keynes-based team until the end of 2028, and before the Dutch Grand Prix this year he penned a new deal keeping him at the team until 2030.

What has he achieved?
It was clear from the early days that Verstappen was going to be an exceptional racing driver and he's become a phenomenon since with a killer instinct.

He's had 244 race starts in F1 and has been on the top step of the podium 71 times. He's been on the podium 131 times and is just two pole positions away from reaching 50 career poles.

The Dutchman has four world championships which he won back-to-back in a dominant Red Bull era between 2021-2024.

He also has an impressive list of achievements to his name, one being in 2023 where he recorded the most wins [19] and the most podium finishes [21] in a single season. He also recorded 10 consecutive race victories.

When is Max vs 100?
The event is taking place on Sept. 16 and will be streamed live on Disney+.

Why is he racing in Max vs 100?

Verstappen has never been shy of getting his teeth stuck into other forms of motorsport away from Formula 1. He most recently made his debut at the iconic Nürburgring 24 Hours in May, driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3.

This will be a slightly different challenge for the Dutchman, but no doubt one he will enjoy with his competitive nature.

"In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking," Verstappen said. "Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it's always nice to return."

The event is taking place at Silverstone in the U.K. and a circuit has been purpose-built for the occasion. It's set to be the biggest go-kart event in the world.

- Max Verstappen deal: Good news for Red Bull and F1, bad news for the driver market

- Max Verstappen ends F1 speculation by signing new Red Bull contract to 2030

How is his 2026 F1 season going?
The 2026 season is one with big regulation and rules changes and Red Bull are currently at the back of the front running teams, but are ahead of the midfield pack.

Verstappen is still searching for his first race win of the season, but has been on the podium four times.

He's currently sixth in the title championship and is 130 points adrift from title leader Kimi Antonelli.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Nashville continue top, Miami bounce back
stories.summary: Lionel Messi's four goals put Miami back on track, while Nashville continue to dominate. All that and more in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, which means it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

Which team looks the strongest coming down the stretch? Who's going to suffer in the dog days of summer? Our writers studied the action from across Matchday 22 to come up with this week's order. Let's dive in.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

A week after setting history (most points in a single MLS season) with a close win over Columbus, Nashville walloped the other Ohio side, FC Cincinnati, 4-0. Cincinnati had more opportunities than the scoreline shows, but Brian Schwake came up big with six saves to keep the clean sheet.

2. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 2

After beating Sporting Kansas City 3-0, Vancouver has two straight clean sheets with games featuring three or more goals. Thomas Müller scored one of those goals and notched an assist in the win, officially moving past Sebastian Berhalter -- who left the club for Middlesbrough this summer -- in the goal charts.

3. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 3

Lionel Messi helped the Herons win easily against Montréal, scoring four goals in a 7-1 thriller that culminated in a beautiful free kick goal to put himself in the lead of the Golden Boot race. After a brief lull post-World Cup, that's three straight games with goals from Miami's No. 10.

4. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

The Fire fired off 20 shots, and outpaced Seattle 11 to three on target, but there's only so much you can do when goalkeeper Andrew Thomas makes nine saves. After settling for a 2-2 draw with the Sounders, Chicago are still five games undefeated in the MLS regular season, despite losing in Leagues Cup midweek.

5. LAFC
Previous ranking: 4

LAFC may have taken 19 shots, but they managed to get just one on target in a 0-0 draw against D.C. United. At the other end, Hugo Lloris made four saves to collect his 11th clean sheet of the season, the most of any player in MLS (LAFC has the most of any team with 12).

6. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 6

Most of Cincinnati's chances came late in a lopsided game, but they produced enough to deserve more than a 4-0 loss to Nashville. The defeat broke a four-game undefeated streak, but hey, there are worse teams to lose to than first-place Nashville.

7. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 9

St. Louis are undefeated in 12 games in MLS after drawing Dallas 3-3. They'll regret dropping the points with two goals conceded after the 81st minute, but they're still a team with some of the hottest form in the league after drawing the Toros.

8. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 11

While playing a team with one of the worst forms in the league, the Revs rose to the occasion with a 3-1 win against the Crew. With a lovely lofted goal toward the end, Carles Gil stretched his goal tally to eight with his first since Aug. 1.

9. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 8

The Pigeons haven't won a game outside of Leagues Cup since July 25, but have two straight 1-1 draws after Saturday's contest against Toronto. Matt Freese did his part with five saves, while Nico Fernández set things off with his 14th goal of the year.

10. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

Jonathan Bond came up big in a 0-0 draw against San Jose, making four saves to collect his 10th clean sheet of the season -- tied for second-most in the league. After snapping their undefeated run last week, a 0-0 draw will do as they prepare for Charlotte.

11. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 12

Minnesota crawled back from a 2-0 deficit and, despite taking a brief lead after scoring three goals in six minutes, settled for a 3-3 draw with Orlando. They deserved more in the final third, but Maxime Crépeau's six saves stood in the way.

12. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 7

After losing 1-0 to Colorado, RSL is winless in eight games in the regular season and have four straight defeats across all competitions. With just 36% possession (compared to their season-long average of 49) and zero shots on target, Salt Lake are looking a bit lost ahead of a meeting with LAFC next week.

13. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

Two first-half goals were all it took to collect three points in a 2-0 win against Atlanta as Charlotte goes four games undefeated in the regular season, and makes it four wins in four games in Atlanta.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

Dallas clawed their way back to a 3-3 draw against St. Louis, who are just below them in the Western Conference and tied on points, thanks to some late-game magic. That includes two goals after the 81st minute and a 97th-minute equalizer from Logan Farrington set up by Petar Musa.

15. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

San Diego welcomed Hirving Lozano to his former home ground with a smattering of boos. Lozano scored, but with the help of CJ dos Santos' six saves, San Diego came away with a 3-1 win to mark their second-straight victory with three goals.

16. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 17

In a respectable 3-3 draw against Minnesota, Daryl Dike made his first start since returning to his former club and scored his first goal. They conceded four goals in four minutes and fumbled the early lead. But with a first goal from Dike and Antoine Griezmann's third goal in two games (fourth of the season) plus a beautiful late assist, the future looks hopeful for ninth-place Orlando.

17. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 18

The Union resurgence continued where it began: with another victory at Sports Illustrated Stadium. In their first game back since beating the Red Bulls there on July 22, Philly beat them 3-1 to bring them to seven games undefeated (five games, two draws) as they continue to battle their way into the playoff spots. Cavan Sullivan's third goal of the year brings him to 10 goal contributions this season, level with Freddy Adu for an MLS record for players aged 16 or younger in the league.

18. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

After four straight defeats, a 0-0 draw against Houston is a respectable result for a team with tumbling form. With Timo Werner added to a lengthening injury list for the game, the result is even more impressive.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 19

Despite delivering a draw against Chicago, RBNY are in a four-game slump (three defeats, one draw) after losing 3-1 to Philadelphia. They missed some chances (including a big one from Julian Hall) and Andre Blake stopped the rest, and will need to recover on a tough four-game road schedule ahead.

20. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 20

Lozano scored his first goal for the Galaxy in his fourth appearance while playing his former club. But that wasn't enough in a 3-1 loss to San Diego. Dos Santos parried away six shots on target in an otherwise even contest.

21. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 21

After an eight-game losing streak, Seattle has two straight draws after tying Chicago 2-2. While Thomas had a masterclass in goal with nine saves, Dejan Joveljic opened his account with two goals in his debut for his new team, after signing from Kansas City last week. Things are looking up.

22. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 22

Dániel Sallói's sixth goal of the season came in a 1-1 draw with NYCFC, which brings Toronto to five games undefeated as they finish the weekend just one spot short of the playoff wildcard spots.

23. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 23

Portland were a bit unlucky at home, as they required a late penalty to break through in a 1-2 defeat to Austin, despite coming out with higher quality opportunities overall. They have two tough games at home (Minnesota and St. Louis) to recover.

24. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 26

D.C.'s 0-0 draw with LAFC was their 10th draw of the season, putting them level with Toronto for most draws in the league. After two straight defeats in the previous weeks, a 0-0 draw is a valiant feat.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 27

Austin absconded with all three points in Portland after beating the Timbers 2-1 with a dramatic 93rd-minute goal from Oleksandr Svatok, the first of the season for the Ukrainian defender.

26. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 24

Right-back Reggie Cannon's second goal of the year was enough to secure three points in a 1-0 win against RSL. They weren't as clinical as they could have been with the opportunities they produced, but they made it count.

27. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 25

After a brief interlude in Leagues Cup (they lost to Club América in the quarterfinal last week), Columbus picked back up with their losing streak in the regular season, stretching it to four straight defeats after losing 3-1 to New England.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 29

Atlanta's three-game winning streak came to a halt against Charlotte. They had a smattering of solid chances, but none broke through, while Charlotte's early goals proved too much to come back from.

29. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 28

Montréal's four-game undefeated run (one win, three draws) came to a roaring halt with a 7-1 collapse against Inter Miami, their first loss since losing to... well, Miami.

30. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 30

SKC has managed the fewest shots on target across all of MLS this season. With their top scorer Joveljic gone (and despite the debut of their big new signing André Luiz in the second half), they kept the streak alive with zero in a 0-3 loss to Vancouver.

stories.headline: Aston Villa's Champions League draw: Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona, Borussia Dortmund
stories.summary: Aston Villa have been handed a tough draw in the league phase of the Champions League with a trip to Barcelona and a home clash against back-to-back winners Paris Saint-Germain.
stories.body:
Aston Villa have been handed a tough draw in the league phase of the Champions League with a trip to Barcelona and a home clash against back-to-back winners Paris Saint-Germain.

Villa will also host German giants Borussia Dortmund and travel to Belgium to face Club Brugge.

Unai Emery's side will host Fenerbahce with a tough away trip to fellow Turkish side Galatasaray also on the agenda.

- Aston Villa sign Leon Goretzka on free transfer

- Premier League 2026-27 kits: Ranking every jersey released

- Is this the iconic Champions League star ball's final season?

Their draw is rounded off with a home tie against Norwegian side Viking and an away clash in Prague against Slavia Prague.

Villa come into this year's competition as Europa League champions after they beat SC Freiburg 3-0 in the final in May.

However, it has been a summer of significant departures at Villa Park with Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans all leaving the club.

Speaking on their Champions League draw, Johan Lange, Aston Villa sporting director said: "Amazing season. Unai Emery has done an amazing job, won the Europa League.

"He has changed a lot of players this season. It seems like he bought exciting, young players. Added some experience as well.

"So it was an exciting draw as well for the fans. The phone is already going mad regarding tickets, you know Barcelona, Paris St Germain. Very interesting, very exciting and I think the club is really excited to be in this competition."

stories.headline: Cris Cyborg is still going strong as a force in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: At age 41, PFL women's featherweight champion continues win streak to secure spot in ESPN P4P top 10.
stories.body:
Cris Cyborg is an MMA legend. Period. End of story.

Actually, the Cyborg story continues, even with her being 41 years old and having spent 21 years in the sport. A champion in an unprecedented five fight promotions, she has long been a fixture in the ESPN pound-for-pound women's rankings. And by posting her 30th career victory -- the most ever by a woman in MMA -- at PFL Tampa on Saturday to retain the women's featherweight championship, Cyborg solidified her hold on the No. 3 spot.

It wasn't easy, not like so many past Cyborg fights in which she aggressively bowled over opponents to score quick knockouts. Ketlen Vieira put up a fight, bloodying Cyborg's face and achieving controlling positions on the canvas several times. But Cyborg persevered, nearly doubling Vieira's strike output and earning a unanimous decision win. As a result, the ESPN voting panel kept her right where she was in the top three.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Aug. 26. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko has more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and now she's established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira on Saturday as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 4

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: TBA

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

6. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-2

Last: W (TKO1) vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius, Oct. 18, 2025

Next: Sept. 12 vs. Alexa Grasso

Fiorot has handled everyone the UFC has put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But Fiorot could earn another shot at the belt if she can get past Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

9. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

10. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 17-5-1

Last: W (KO) vs. Maycee Barber, March 28

Next: Sept. 12 vs. Manon Fiorot

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. That made the fight with Barber a must-win, and Grasso came through explosively. Next up is Fiorot, a fellow title contender.

Other fighter receiving votes: Virna Jandiroba.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Manon Fiorot; 6. Dakota Ditcheva; 7. Natalia Silva; 8. Erin Blanchfield; 9. Tatiana Suarez; 10. Virna Jandiroba.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Ditcheva; 5. Dern; 6. Silva; 7. Alexa Grasso; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Fiorot; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Ditcheva; 9. Suarez; 10. Jandiroba.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Fiorot; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Grasso.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Fiorot; 5. Silva; 6. Dern; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Suarez; 9. Ditcheva; 10. Grasso.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Where does Aspinall go from here?

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

Other fighters receiving votes: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan.

How our panel voted

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Pantoja; 6. Gaethje; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Van.

stories.headline: Sharks skipper McInnes: NRL changes rules at 'the drop of a hat'
stories.summary: Cameron McInnes wouldn't be surprised to see the NRL deny Cronulla a home final at Shark Park, warning players were now used to head office making rule changes "at the drop of a hat".
stories.body:
Cameron McInnes wouldn't be surprised to see the NRL deny Cronulla a home final at Shark Park, warning players were now used to head office making rule changes "at the drop of a hat".

Out of form on the eve of finals, the fifth-placed Sharks are nevertheless guaranteed to host a week-one elimination match against one of South Sydney, North Queensland or Newcastle.

But the finals suitability of dilapidated Shark Park, the NRL's lowest-capacity regular venue at 15,000 seats, has been a discussion point in recent years.

The NRL pockets ticket sales from finals games so would take a financial hit from hosting in the Shire rather than Allianz Stadium or Accor Stadium, which each have more than twice the capacity.

Shark Park has been deemed unfit for use in week two or three of the finals, but hosted week-one finals matches in 2022, 2023 and 2025.

The NRL is unlikely to publicly confirm venues until after round 27 finishes this Sunday, and told clubs in the preseason it had the discretion to determine where finals games were played.

The possibility of playing elsewhere did not sit well with England-bound McInnes, who could be playing his last game at Shark Park against Melbourne this Saturday.

"I was under the impression the rule was if you earn a home semi, whether you're first or second, or fifth or sixth, you get to play it at your home. Our home is Shark Park," he said.

"I don't know if that was a rule change that they can just put in, but then again, the NRL changes rules all the time.

"Rule changes just happen at the drop of a hat now, don't they? So as a player, you just have to adapt."

The league most recently trialled a change to the kick-off rule in Melbourne's defeat of Brisbane last week, having introduced six-agains, 20/40 kicks, two-point field goals and captain's challenges since the start of the decade.

The NRL has also made less prominent changes to its trainer and interchange policies in that time, as well as reverting to one on-field referee per game.

"How much do you need to change? I understand at the end of the day, it's entertainment, I get it," McInnes said.

"But it's like someone's constantly sitting there going, 'The game's going really well, but now let's change something else'."

Inconsistency around ruck infringements was most dismaying to veteran McInnes, who sympathised with the league's match officials.

"When you bring that (six-again rule) in, I get it, to speed the game up and have the speeds to score long-range tries with fatigue, but it also creates an inconsistency in the game," he said.

"(It's) hard for the refs, isn't it? Because it's so subjective.

"If someone gets hit in the face and is offside, that's clear as day, but with the six-agains, it's just sort of a lottery."
